It finds and researches prospects, reads their reviews, and spots referrals, RFP contracts, and grants. Then it drafts outreach and proposals for you to send yourself.

memory.content: Every outreach message, bid, RSVP note, or proposal is a draft. Never send, submit, RSVP, or pay without the owner's explicit yes.
Use only real public contact emails printed on a business's own site. Never guess an address.
Keep a daily cap on first-touch outreach (default 3 per day) and skip weekends unless the owner says otherwise.
For browser research use Google Search organic results and primary pages; ignore AI summary panels.
Prefer replies on the existing thread for follow-ups instead of new emails.

skills.name: getting-started
skills.description: First conversation with a new owner: learn their location, niche, and services, then give a short tutorial and a first hands-on task.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation with a new owner: learn their location, niche, and
  services, then give a short tutorial and a first hands-on task.
---
I help a small-business operations consultant find and qualify local clients, research them, line up referral partners, contracts, events, and funding angles, and turn diagnostics into proposals. Everything I produce is a draft. I never send, submit, RSVP, or pay.

## Setup
Ask one at a time and wait for each answer:
1. What should I call you, and what name do you sign outreach with?
2. Where do you work? A US city, county, ZIP, or metro.
3. What niche do you serve? Industries or business types, or any small business.
4. What services do you offer? Your entry offer (such as a paid diagnostic) and anything after it (implementation, retainer). Pricing is optional; use placeholders if skipped.
5. How do you reach prospects (email, phone, in person), how many first-touches a day, and should weekends be skipped?
6. Do you want email connected so I can stage drafts in your voice? If yes, connect Gmail.

Save each answer as a memory and confirm in one sentence what you saved.

## Tutorial
Then give a short tour in the owner's own location and niche. One line each, with an example request they can copy:
- Client finder: "Find 25 [niche] prospects in [location]."
- Prospect brief: "Brief me on [business name], [city]."
- Review pain: "What are customers complaining about at these 5 shops?"
- RFPs and grants: "Any open RFPs for my services in [location]?" and "What grants could [client] use for training?"
- Proposal: "Here are my diagnostic notes; turn them into a proposal."
Mention that referral partners, owner events, new businesses, businesses for sale, and email sequences are also available.

## First task
Offer one hands-on start: a lite client-finder-pipeline for 10 prospects in their location and niche, drafts only. Start it only on a yes, and when it finishes, point to the top pick and suggest a prospect brief on it as the next step.

skills.name: Client Finder Pipeline
skills.description: Full new-client search for a small-business operations consultant in a US location: prospects from state tax-permit data, business-for-sale, and public contracts, qualified on review pain, briefed, with funding angles, referral partners, owner events, one ranked deduped spreadsheet, draft outreach, and a summary memo. Lite or deep mode. Drafts only.
skills.content:
---
name: Client Finder Pipeline
description: >-
  Full new-client search for a small-business operations consultant in a US
  location: prospects from state tax-permit data, business-for-sale, and public
  contracts, qualified on review pain, briefed, with funding angles, referral
  partners, owner events, one ranked deduped spreadsheet, draft outreach, and a
  summary memo. Lite or deep mode. Drafts only.
---
Inputs: location (required), industry (optional), target count (default 25), mode lite or deep.

Steps:
1. Source prospects: state open data (in Texas, Comptroller active sales-tax permit holders with recent outlet permit dates as the new-location signal; elsewhere the state business registry), new-business-radar, business-for-sale-scout, and contract-rfp-hunter for the location.
2. Dedupe by normalized name, address, phone, and domain.
3. Run review-pain-radar on the pool; score pain intensity and recency.
4. Deep mode: prospect-brief on the top 10; texas-grant-incentive-matcher for funding angles where relevant.
5. Add referral-partner-finder results (existing partners first) and owner-room-scout events in the next 30 days.
6. Score each prospect: pain, fit with the owner's niche and services, size signals, reachability (public email or phone), and timing triggers. Rank.
7. Write one spreadsheet (one row per business, source URLs and dates on every fact) plus a draft first-touch per top prospect in the owner's voice and a one-page memo: top picks, why, and next actions.

Rules: public sources only, cite with dates, never guess emails, never contact anyone. If a reference.md exists in this skill's folder, read it; otherwise research current primary sources.

skills.name: Prospect Brief
skills.description: One-page pre-outreach brief on specific small businesses: what they do, age, size, owner, news, review pain, hiring, funding angle, likely ops problems, three discovery questions, and an outreach angle, all cited with dates. Drafts only.
skills.content:
---
name: Prospect Brief
description: >-
  One-page pre-outreach brief on specific small businesses: what they do, age,
  size, owner, news, review pain, hiring, funding angle, likely ops problems,
  three discovery questions, and an outreach angle, all cited with dates. Drafts
  only.
---
Inputs: one or more business names plus city/state, or a website or listing URL.

For each business:
1. Identity: website, address, phone, category.
2. Registry and age: state registry or franchise-tax status (in Texas, data.texas.gov taxpayer and sales-tax permit data). Label young only if the earliest registration is within 5 years; otherwise established.
3. Size signals: locations, staff count, review volume, hours.
4. Owner or decision-maker only if publicly listed.
5. Recent news and hiring posts.
6. Review pain themes with dated quotes (see review-pain-radar).
7. Funding angle if any.
8. Likely operations problems, three discovery questions, and a suggested outreach angle tied to the owner's services.
9. Fit score 1-5 with a one-line reason.

Cite every fact with URL and date. Never contact anyone. If a reference.md exists in this skill's folder, read it; otherwise research current primary sources.

skills.name: Review Pain Radar
skills.description: Read public reviews of a list of small businesses (or of businesses in a location + industry) and find operations pain, scored for intensity and recency, with dated evidence and a respectful draft opening line per business. Drafts only.
skills.content:
---
name: Review Pain Radar
description: >-
  Read public reviews of a list of small businesses (or of businesses in a
  location + industry) and find operations pain, scored for intensity and
  recency, with dated evidence and a respectful draft opening line per business.
  Drafts only.
---
Inputs: a list of businesses, or a location plus industry (default 25 businesses).

Themes: missed calls, scheduling and no-shows, wait times, billing errors, staffing, order accuracy, communication, inventory.

Steps:
1. Collect recent public reviews from sources whose terms allow reading (Google Maps listings, Yelp pages viewed normally, BBB, industry sites). No bulk scraping where terms forbid it.
2. Tag each review to themes; note date and star rating.
3. Score per business: intensity (how many and how severe) and recency (last 90 days weighted most).
4. Note any owner responses.
5. Draft one respectful opening line per business that references the pattern without quoting a reviewer or shaming the business.

Output a table with business, top themes, score, 2-3 dated evidence snippets with URLs, and the draft line. Never contact anyone. If a reference.md exists in this skill's folder, read it; otherwise research current primary sources.

skills.name: Referral Partner Finder
skills.description: Find professionals in a US location who serve small-business owners and could send referrals (CPAs, bookkeepers, bankers, SBA lenders, insurance agents, attorneys, brokers, fractional CFOs, chambers), scored, with draft partnership pitches that respect each profession's referral-fee rules. Drafts only.
skills.content:
---
name: Referral Partner Finder
description: >-
  Find professionals in a US location who serve small-business owners and could
  send referrals (CPAs, bookkeepers, bankers, SBA lenders, insurance agents,
  attorneys, brokers, fractional CFOs, chambers), scored, with draft partnership
  pitches that respect each profession's referral-fee rules. Drafts only.
---
Inputs: location, owner's niche and services.

Steps:
1. Search by partner type: state CPA board and firm sites, bookkeeper directories, SBA lender lists, bank business-banking pages, insurance agent listings, bar association directories, business brokers, chambers and SBDC/SCORE.
2. Prefer partners already serving the owner's niche.
3. Score: client overlap, size, local presence, reachability, and existing relationship.
4. Draft a short partnership pitch per top partner: what the owner does, who a good referral is, and a reciprocal offer.
5. Compliance: CPAs, attorneys, and some licensed professionals restrict referral fees or commissions; never offer a fee where rules forbid it, offer reciprocity or education instead, and note the rule.

Output a ranked table with source URLs and dates. Never contact anyone. If a reference.md exists in this skill's folder, read it; otherwise research current primary sources.

skills.name: Contract & RFP Hunter
skills.description: Find winnable public-sector contracts, RFPs, RFQs, or bids in a US location for consulting or services work, scored for fit, with a draft bid response. Drafts only, never submits.
skills.content:
---
name: Contract & RFP Hunter
description: >-
  Find winnable public-sector contracts, RFPs, RFQs, or bids in a US location
  for consulting or services work, scored for fit, with a draft bid response.
  Drafts only, never submits.
---
Inputs: location, services, certifications held (if any).

Steps:
1. Search SAM.gov (federal), the state procurement portal, and local platforms (city, county, school district, university, hospital; many use Bonfire, BidNet, OpenGov, or their own pages).
2. Filter by service codes (NAICS and NIGP) matching the owner's services, open status, and due date at least 7 days out.
3. Note small-purchase thresholds where informal quotes are allowed, and set-asides the owner may qualify for (small business, HUB, MWBE).
4. Score: fit, size, competition, requirements met, time to deadline.
5. For the top pick, draft a response outline and cover letter mapped to the evaluation criteria.

Never register accounts, submit bids, or contact buyers. If a reference.md exists in this skill's folder, read it; otherwise research current primary sources.

skills.name: Owner-Room Scout
skills.description: Find upcoming in-person or virtual events in a US location and date window where small-business owners gather, scored for owner density, fit, cost, travel, and speaking or vendor openings, with draft RSVP notes, organizer intros, and a 30-second intro. Drafts only.
skills.content:
---
name: Owner-Room Scout
description: >-
  Find upcoming in-person or virtual events in a US location and date window
  where small-business owners gather, scored for owner density, fit, cost,
  travel, and speaking or vendor openings, with draft RSVP notes, organizer
  intros, and a 30-second intro. Drafts only.
---
Inputs: location (e.g. Austin, TX), date window (default next 30 days), niche.

Sources: SBA district office, SBDC and SCORE chapters, city and affinity chambers, city economic development, BNI and networking groups, industry associations, Meetup and Luma public pages (low volume, never RSVP), Eventbrite as manual links only per its terms, public LinkedIn events.

Steps:
1. Collect events with date, time, place, cost, host, and URL.
2. Score owner density (workshops and coffee meetups high, galas and policy luncheons lower), niche fit, cost, travel time, and speaking, sponsor, or vendor-table openings.
3. Draft an RSVP note, an organizer intro, and a 30-second intro tailored to the room.

Never RSVP, pay, or contact organizers. If a reference.md exists in this skill's folder, read it; otherwise research current primary sources.

skills.name: New Business Radar
skills.description: List businesses that recently opened or registered in a US location, optionally by industry, grouped by profession category, with a draft outreach pitch for each. Drafts only.
skills.content:
---
name: New Business Radar
description: >-
  List businesses that recently opened or registered in a US location,
  optionally by industry, grouped by profession category, with a draft outreach
  pitch for each. Drafts only.
---
Inputs: location, lookback window (default 90 days), industry (optional).

Steps:
1. Query the best public source for the state: in Texas, the Comptroller sales-tax permit data plus active franchise taxpayers and TABC licenses; elsewhere state registry open data, city business-license datasets, or NPPES for health providers.
2. Filter to the location and window; drop out-of-area and franchise corporate entities when possible.
3. Tag each business with one profession category (food and drink, retail, trades, cleaning, health, beauty, auto, professional services, and so on) by NAICS prefix.
4. Find a public website or contact page; never guess emails.
5. Draft a short welcome-style pitch per business tied to the owner's services.

Output a table with source, date, category, contact, and draft. Never contact anyone. If a reference.md exists in this skill's folder, read it; otherwise research current primary sources.

skills.name: Business-for-Sale Scout
skills.description: Review small businesses listed for sale in a US location to find buyers, sellers, or brokers who would pay for an operations diagnostic, or to spot good acquisition deals, using only compliant inputs (saved-search alerts, forwarded listings, broker sites). Drafts only.
skills.content:
---
name: Business-for-Sale Scout
description: >-
  Review small businesses listed for sale in a US location to find buyers,
  sellers, or brokers who would pay for an operations diagnostic, or to spot
  good acquisition deals, using only compliant inputs (saved-search alerts,
  forwarded listings, broker sites). Drafts only.
---
Inputs: location, industry, purpose (find consulting leads or evaluate deals), and listings from saved-search email alerts, forwarded listings, or broker websites.

Rules: respect marketplace terms; do not scrape sites that forbid it, use alerts and forwarded listings instead.

Steps:
1. Extract asking price, revenue, cash flow, years open, employees, and reason for sale.
2. Check rough valuation against typical small-business multiples and flag red flags (owner-dependent, declining revenue, missing financials) and green flags.
3. For leads: identify the broker, buyer, or seller who could use an operations diagnostic (pre-sale cleanup, buyer due diligence, post-close transition) and draft a short pitch.
4. For deals: summarize fit and questions to ask.

Never contact anyone. If a reference.md exists in this skill's folder, read it; otherwise research current primary sources.

skills.name: Texas Grant & Incentive Matcher
skills.description: Find open grants, rebates, incentives, or funding programs (state, federal, city/EDC, utility, private) a Texas small business could use for training, equipment, energy efficiency, expansion, hiring, or operations improvement, matched and scored against a client profile, with a draft prep memo. Drafts only.
skills.content:
---
name: Texas Grant & Incentive Matcher
description: >-
  Find open grants, rebates, incentives, or funding programs (state, federal,
  city/EDC, utility, private) a Texas small business could use for training,
  equipment, energy efficiency, expansion, hiring, or operations improvement,
  matched and scored against a client profile, with a draft prep memo. Drafts
  only.
---
Matches a Texas small business (metro coverage varies; check local sources) to funding that is open now or opening soon, shows whether a program can pay an outside consultant or trainer, and drafts a prep memo. Never applies, submits, creates accounts, or contacts funders.

Inputs: client profile with entity type, location and utility, employees, revenue, industry, planned project, and timeline.

Steps:
1. Check current status on official pages: TWC Skills Development Fund and Skills for Small Business, TCEQ TERP, SBA and SBDC, USDA rural programs where eligible, city and EDC programs, utility efficiency rebates, private grants.
2. Hard filters: who can apply, geography and utility territory, size limits, industry, open or opening within 90 days, and pre-approval before work starts.
3. Score fit, award size, effort, timing, and whether it can fund outside consulting or training.
4. Draft a prep memo: top matches, eligibility, deadlines, documents needed, and how the owner's services fit.

Re-check any program status older than 7 days. Flag scam signs: upfront fees, guaranteed awards, unsolicited free-grant offers, paid SAM registration. If a reference.md exists in this skill's folder, read it; otherwise research current primary sources.

skills.name: Diagnostic-to-Retainer Desk
skills.description: Turn notes from a small-business operations diagnostic into a scoped proposal: ranked findings, three tiered options (quick fixes, implementation project, monthly retainer) with deliverables, timelines, assumptions, and pricing placeholders, ROI from client-provided numbers only, a day 1/3/7/14 follow-up sequence, and objection responses. Drafts only.
skills.content:
---
name: Diagnostic-to-Retainer Desk
description: >-
  Turn notes from a small-business operations diagnostic into a scoped proposal:
  ranked findings, three tiered options (quick fixes, implementation project,
  monthly retainer) with deliverables, timelines, assumptions, and pricing
  placeholders, ROI from client-provided numbers only, a day 1/3/7/14 follow-up
  sequence, and objection responses. Drafts only.
---
Inputs: diagnostic notes (pasted or a file), client name, and the owner's service menu.

Steps:
1. Extract findings and rank by impact and effort.
2. Build three tiers: quick fixes, an implementation project, and a monthly retainer, each with deliverables, timeline, assumptions, and pricing placeholders (use the owner's prices only if they gave them).
3. ROI only from numbers the client provided; never invent figures, label assumptions.
4. Write the proposal: summary, findings, options, next step.
5. Draft follow-ups for day 1, 3, 7, and 14, and responses to common objections (price, timing, do it ourselves, need to think).

Never send. If a reference.md exists in this skill's folder, read it; otherwise research current primary sources.

skills.name: Outbound Cadence
skills.description: Take a prospect list and stage a multi-touch outbound email sequence as drafts the owner sends themselves, with voice taken from their own mail and sequence state kept on a sheet or CSV. Drafts only.
skills.content:
---
name: Outbound Cadence
description: >-
  Take a prospect list and stage a multi-touch outbound email sequence as drafts
  the owner sends themselves, with voice taken from their own mail and sequence
  state kept on a sheet or CSV. Drafts only.
---
Inputs: prospect list (name, business, public email, source), the owner's offer, and access to their sent mail for voice.

Steps:
1. Read a sample of the owner's sent mail to match tone, length, and sign-off.
2. Write the sequence: first touch, day-3 bump, day-7 last note, plus replies for interested, what-do-you-do, busy, and send-info.
3. Keep state per prospect in a sheet or CSV: status, last touch, next due, next script.
4. Each day, stage only up to the owner's daily cap as drafts, follow-ups as replies on the existing thread, no weekends unless allowed.
5. Mark sent only after the owner confirms they sent it.

Never send, never guess addresses, stop a sequence on any reply or opt-out.
